visual.general_description: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram printed as two columns of six leads on pink dotted grid paper.
visual.detailed_description: Left column, top to bottom: I, II, III, aVR, aVL, aVF; right column: V1 to V6. Lead names are printed in blue and a calibration pulse sits at the left of each row; no gain, paper-speed, rate, patient identifier or date text is printed. About three beats are shown per lead. Lead I shows a broad upright QRS followed by a shallow downward deflection below baseline before returning to baseline. Lead II has a small initial upward then deep downward QRS; III, aVR and aVF are mainly negative; aVL has an upright QRS. V1 to V3 show a deep negative QRS followed by an upward-sloping ST-T wave; V4 is deeply negative and larger; V5 and V6 show broad tall upright QRS complexes followed by downward-sloping ST segments and a small upright T deflection. No arrows or annotations are drawn.
